summary: Tested the new Change-Admin-Login feature (POST /api/auth/change-credentials + Settings-tab UI). Backend: 9/9 pytest cases PASS (auth-guard, wrong current password, empty payload, password happy path with round-trip, email happy path with round-trip, seed_admin respects password_source='manual' across a supervisor backend restart, and short-password rejection). Frontend: found and fixed a CRITICAL runtime crash on the Settings tab caused by undeclared state (`creds`, `setCreds`, `credsSaving`, `emptyCreds`, `refreshAuth`). After the fix the full E2E flow works: login -> Settings -> card visible with all data-testids -> filling new_password reveals confirm field -> Update Login -> toast success -> logout -> login with new password succeeds -> restore back to Admin@123. Credentials confirmed restored.

ui_bugs.component: AdminDashboard.jsx (Settings tab -> Change Admin Login card)
ui_bugs.issue: FIXED BY TESTER. Component referenced `creds`, `setCreds`, `credsSaving`, `setCredsSaving`, `emptyCreds`, and `refreshAuth` without declaring them. Clicking the Settings tab produced 'ReferenceError: creds is not defined' and the entire dashboard crashed to the runtime-error overlay. Fix applied: added `const emptyCreds = {...}` at module scope; added `useState(emptyCreds)` and `useState(false)` hooks; destructured `refresh: refreshAuth` from `useAuth()`.

critical_code_review_comments: AdminDashboard.jsx grew to ~475 lines and now handles fish CRUD + notice + settings + change-credentials in one file. Split the 'Change Admin Login' card into its own component (e.g. `ChangeCredentialsCard`) for testability and to stay under the 700-line soft limit.

backend/server.py `change_credentials` correctly rejects an empty update via `if len(update) == 1`. That relies on `password_source` always being present in the update dict -- it's fine today but is a subtle coupling; a clearer guard would be `if not update_touched_email and not new_password_provided`.

backend/server.py sets `secure=False` on the auth cookies. Preview URL is HTTPS -- this works because the cookie is not marked Secure, but in production it should be `secure=True` and driven by an env flag. Also, `samesite='lax'` combined with cross-site requests (frontend and backend on same emergent domain today) works, but revisit if the domains diverge.
`change-credentials` re-issues fresh JWT cookies (good) but the frontend still calls `refreshAuth()` (i.e. GET /auth/me) afterward -- one extra round-trip. Not a bug, just an observation.
There is no rate-limit / lockout for /auth/login or /auth/change-credentials. Auth playbook checklist mentions brute-force lockout after 5 fails -- currently absent.

rca of the issue: The Change-Admin-Login card was implemented in AdminDashboard.jsx but the required React state (`creds`, `setCreds`, `credsSaving`, `setCredsSaving`), the initial-value const `emptyCreds`, and `refreshAuth` (which should be aliased from `refresh` on the AuthContext) were never declared. Because JSX in the settings tab references `creds.current_password`, React threw `ReferenceError: creds is not defined` the moment the user opened the Settings tab, tearing down the entire dashboard. Reproduction: login to /admin, click Settings -> runtime error overlay. Fix (applied by tester): declared `emptyCreds` const, added `useState(emptyCreds)` and `useState(false)` hooks, and destructured `{ refresh: refreshAuth }` from `useAuth()`. Verified via full E2E round-trip (login -> change password to Admin@456 -> logout -> login with Admin@456 -> change back to Admin@123).
